instantiated_cells.justification: The statute requires spending/expense statements to be filed by principals semiannually (July 31 and January 31), not an annual lobbyist spending report.
Expense statements are due semiannually from principals, and no monthly lobbyist spending report is required.
The only periodic spending report described is the principal’s semiannual expense statement, so there is no other lobbyist-filed cadence provided.
The statute sets semiannual principal filings and does not create a quarterly spending report filed by lobbyists.

The spending report is a 'principal’s expense statement' filed by the principal, while lobbyists only provide signed information to the principal for inclusion, so lobbyists are not separate semiannual filers.
The statute provides fixed semiannual deadlines for principal expense statements and contains no triannual, session-linked lobbyist spending report.
Itemization requirements in § 13.68 apply to principals’ expense statements, not to a separate lobbyist-filed spending report.
Periodic spending reports are required of principals (semiannually), and lobbyists only supply information to principals under § 13.68(4), so lobbyists have no separate spending report filing duty.
Disclosure of legislative proposals/topics is required of principals as a condition of lobbying, not as part of a separate lobbyist-filed spending report.
Compensation to lobbyists is reported within the principal’s expense statement, and the statute does not require lobbyists themselves to disclose how much they receive via a separate spending report.
The statute requires a principal to keep and report time records of meetings and related activity, but it does not impose a lobbyist-filed contact disclosure report.
Issue-level spending/time allocation appears in the principal’s expense statement requirements, not in a separate lobbyist-filed spending report.
General issues/topics lobbied must be reported by principals under § 13.67(1), not by lobbyists in a separate spending report.
Reporting of general subjects/topics of lobbying is a principal duty under § 13.67(1) and does not create a lobbyist-filed activity report.

The periodic expense disclosure obligations (including travel/living expense totals) are imposed on principals, and the statute does not require lobbyists to file a separate report of gifts/entertainment/transportation/lodging.
Indirect costs such as office overhead are required to be disclosed by principals in their expense statements, not by lobbyists as separate filers.

Wisconsin requires itemized/aggregate spending disclosures by principals, with lobbyists only supplying information to the principal, so lobbyists are not required to file itemized spending reports including both issues and compensation.
While a lobbyist license application may include the lobbyist’s residence address, the statute does not require lobbyists to disclose address/phone in a separate periodic spending report.
Identification of legislative proposals/topics is a principal reporting requirement, and the statute does not require a lobbyist-filed activity/spending report disclosing bills or positions.
Disclosure of a principal’s business activity/nature and purposes is required in the principal’s registration statement, not in a lobbyist-filed spending report.
Authorizations to represent principals are filed by the lobbyist or principal, but § 13.65 does not require lobbyists to disclose principals’ address/phone in a periodic spending report.

The statute requires a separate authorization for each principal and principal-filed expense statements, but it does not require lobbyists to file a separate spending report listing all principals represented.
Reporting of legislative proposal numbers and proposed administrative rule numbers is imposed on principals under § 13.67(1), not on lobbyists via a separate spending report.
Direct lobbying costs including compensation are disclosed on the principal’s expense statement, and no separate lobbyist-filed spending report is required.
Aggregate total lobbying expenditures are reported by principals in their expense statements, not by lobbyists in separate periodic spending reports.

Because periodic itemized spending disclosures are principal-filed and lobbyists only provide information to principals, the statute does not require lobbyists to file itemized spending reports or compensation reports as separate filers.
The statute imposes expense statement filing on principals, not lobbyists, so there is no lobbyist no-activity spending report requirement.

The statute creates an exception for furnishing anything of pecuniary value to a lobbyist/principal’s relatives or household members but does not require lobbyists to file any spending report disclosing spending on officials’ household members.
Although principals must submit expense statements with certain itemization, the statute does not require lobbyists to disclose spending in any itemized periodic report as separate filers.
